title: Automated safeguard for client-side feature flag rollouts with rollback simulations
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: We need a consistent, automated mechanism to perform progressive rollouts for changes that depend on client-side feature flags (including model variant flips and routing policy changes) across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Current processes rely on manual ramp scripts and human-monitored canaries which are slow and inconsistent, and they do not simulate rollback impact prior to wide release.

Goal: Build an "automated safeguard" system that: (1) executes rehearsals (dry-run rollback simulations) in staging and small cohorts in prod, (2) computes a composite health score for each cohort using latency/error/quality/cost signals, (3) proposes a safe ramp schedule and automatically pauses or rolls back when thresholds are violated, and (4) integrates with our feature-flag backend so product/PMs can initiate controlled flips with a single workflow. This must work for hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) with appropriate RBAC and audit logs.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable rollout policy can be attached to any client-side flag flip and persisted in the rollout policy store
The system performs a staging rehearsal that simulates rollback and reports expected rollback surface (sessions, KV cache warmup cost, latency spike risk)
A composite health score is calculated per cohort and documented; rollout halts automatically when score falls below policy thresholds
Automatic rollback can be executed without manual intervention and is recorded in audit logs with reason and metrics snapshot
Integration with Redwood Console: per-flag rollout dashboard and per-cohort traces available; alerts created in PagerDuty for P0 thresholds
Works for Dedicated and Private customers subject to their RBAC constraints (agent + control-plane choreography)
implementation_notes:
Architecture: rollout-orchestrator service will coordinate rehearsals, cohort creation, health scoring, and rollback actions. It will consult a policy DSL stored in the rollout-policy store. For client-side flags, orchestrator will call the feature-flag service API to create cohorts and gradual percentage rules. For Dedicated/Private, orchestrator will emit operations to the deployment agent (via control-plane connector) rather than direct flag flips.

Health scoring: combine p95 latency delta, 5xx/error-rate delta, model-quality regression from a lightweight canary-eval set, KV cache miss-rate, and cost per token. Score is a weighted sum; weights will be configurable per-project.

Dry-run rollback: run in staging against production-like traffic replay for the changed flag path. The rehearsal should produce an estimate of the rollback wall-time (cache cold-start penalty) and a predicted transient latency spike distribution.

Safety hooks: include manual hold window, automatic pace limiter (max % increase per minute), and cooldown windows after each step. Expose an API for on-call to force immediate rollback or pin cohorts.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design & policy DSL (2 sprints) - finalize rollout-policy schema and weights for composite health score
Phase 1: Staging rehearsal engine (1 sprint) - implement traffic-replay and dry-run rollback estimator
Phase 2: Orchestrator + FF integration (2 sprints) - safe flips for hosted; agent connector for Dedicated/Private
Phase 3: Console integration & runbooks (1 sprint) - dashboard, notify/alerts, and on-call runbook
Phase 4: Pilot with 2 product teams (2 weeks) - iterate policies and thresholds
Phase 5: GA and docs (1 sprint) - public docs, SDK examples, template policies
metrics_and_triggers: Primary metrics: p95 latency delta (cohort vs baseline), 5xx rate delta, model-quality regression % on canary-eval set
Secondary metrics: KV cache miss-rate, GPU utilization delta, tokens-per-second cost delta
Automatic pause trigger: composite health score < 0.75 for 3 consecutive minutes
Automatic rollback trigger: composite health score < 0.6 OR 5xx rate > baseline*3 sustained for 2 minutes
Notify (but do not rollback) trigger: p95 latency delta > 30% for single minute
Safety cap: never ramp more than 20% of total traffic in a single 10-minute window unless manual override is provided
notes:
Operational concerns: for Private deployments where control-plane operations are restricted, the pilot will require a local agent update and a signed operator runbook. We should validate collection of model-quality signals from private clusters (may require additional telemetry opt-in).

Decision log: prefer an external orchestrator service vs embedding in feature-flag service to keep scope limited and allow reuse across non-flag rollouts (model-only switches, routing policy changes). We will store audit trails in the existing audit-log pipeline to satisfy compliance requirements.

Open questions: how to set initial default weights for composite score (proposal: start with latency 30%, errors 35%, quality 25%, cost 10%) and whether to let product teams override per-rollout. Also need to confirm exact cost delta calculation for multi-model A/Bs.
